key_insight: HarnessPro recursively improves AI-agent harnesses to offer performance–cost trade-offs, with its heavy mode outperforming RHO while reducing execution cost.
engineering_relevance: Engineers can select lite, medium, or heavy harnesses to match deployment budgets rather than optimize task success alone.
method: Evaluate candidate harnesses with LLM-generated tests, without ground-truth solutions or official tests.
Use specialized agents to diagnose execution traces, plan performance–cost updates, and implement candidates.
Select lite, medium, and heavy variants using normalized weighted squared distance, then iterate with execution feedback.
evidence_signal: Across Terminal-Bench 2, SWE-Bench Pro, and ProgramBench with GPT-5.5 and Codex, heavy mode averages a 2.0-percentage-point pass-rate gain and 26.1% lower per-task cost versus RHO; the abstract also reports an advantage with GLM-5.2 and Claude Code.
watch_item: LLM-generated tests may miss real task requirements, so label-free optimization needs independent validation before deployment.
paper_title: HarnessPro: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement with Pareto Optimization for Performance-Cost Trade-offs
